lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: Radius 6, central angle 60°. Arc and sector?
A cyclic quadrilateral has an angle of 85°. Opposite angle?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 54°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 5. From an external point 13 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 8, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
12, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
12, because the tangent bisects the radius
18, because the tangent extends beyond the circle

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 60°, in terms of π.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 117°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 104°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 3. From an external point 5 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 4, because the tangent bisects the radius
8, because the tangent extends beyond the circle
4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
2, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

items.prompt: A circle has radius 13. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 90°, in terms of π.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 41°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 62°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
